Subject: Re: Post-call recap + security/compliance follow-ups (SOC 2, retention, vendor questionnaire)

Leah / Samir — thanks. Attaching our short SOC 2 status summary and a filled vendor questionnaire for your review (see attachments). Summary below and answers to the retention questions.

SOC 2 status:
- Current: Redwood has completed SOC 2 Type I historically and is conducting the Type II audit cycle this year.
- Expected Type II completion: Q3 2027 (anticipated audit window July–August).
- Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf (controls overview + scope). For detailed evidence we can grant a time-bound Drive link and set up an NDA if you prefer.

Data retention & deletion (hosted API defaults):
- Primary customer data (user-provided content): deleted within 30 days after a confirmed deletion request. Deletion removes accessible primary copies and associated application metadata.
- Embeddings & KV cache: treated as customer data; removed within 30 days of deletion request. We also scrub in-memory caches immediately upon request where feasible.
- Service logs (audit / operational logs): default retention 90 days. Can be reduced or extended for Dedicated/Private deployments by contract.
- Backups / snapshots: retained for disaster recovery up to 180 days by default. Backups are subject to regular overwrite cycles; deletion requests mark data for purge from primary systems, and backups are removed during the next scheduled retention cycle (within the 180-day window). For expedited purges we offer an enterprise option (contract addendum) that accelerates backup scrubbing.

GDPR/HIPAA:
- GDPR: We support DSAR workflows. Data subject erasure requests are handled per the deletion SLA above; we can provide a playbook for DSARs on request.
- HIPAA: We support HIPAA via Dedicated and Private deployments. A BAA is available for customers with appropriate deployment choices and contractual terms.

Next steps we can take this week:
1) Neha will share the completed vendor questionnaire (attached).
2) Rishi can run through retention specifics and provide a short one-page retention SLA we can attach to procurement.
3) If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with our Security PM and infra lead — Rishi is available Tue/Wed next week.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf, Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_filled.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks for the detail — that helps. A few clarifying questions before procurement:

1) Embeddings / KV caches: when you say "removed within 30 days", does that mean the data is rendered unrecoverable immediately (e.g., crypto-delete) or marked for deletion and then purged on next backup cycle? Is there a distinction between user-initiated deletions and automated retention expiries?
2) Backups: can you provide more detail on the snapshot cadence and whether backups are incremental or full? Our procurement team needs to understand whether PHI could persist in backups beyond the deletion window and whether an expedited scrub option is contractually available.
3) Logs: if we require a shorter log window (e.g., 30 days), can that be set on your hosted tier or only on Dedicated/Private?

Also — can Rishi or Neha join a brief walkthrough with our security team next week? We'd like to go line-by-line through the questionnaire.

Leah

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Leah Gordon <leah.gordon@amaya.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@amaya.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + security/compliance follow-ups (SOC 2, retention, vendor questionnaire)

Leah — great questions, appreciate the specificity. Below are direct answers; happy to review on a call.

1) Embeddings / KV caches:
- Deletion semantics: for Hosted API, a deletion request flags customer data for immediate logical deletion from the application layer; embedded indices and KV caches are scrubbed from active stores within 24–72 hours where possible. For cryptographic shredding (making data cryptographically unrecoverable) we perform crypto-delete on eligible storage classes; however, for backups there is the backup retention caveat below.
- User-initiated deletions vs automated expiries: both follow the same logical deletion process. Automated expiries (e.g., TTL) are enforced by the retention engine and may result in scheduled purges.

2) Backups / snapshots:
- Cadence: backups are incremental daily with weekly full snapshots by default. Backups are stored encrypted at rest.
- Persistence: because backups are incremental, deleted data may exist in older incremental segments until those segments are rotated out. Our default rotation is 180 days.
- Expedited scrub: we provide an enterprise add-on for expedited backup scrubbing that replaces the default retention timeline; this is available under Dedicated/Private or as a contractual SLA for Hosted at enterprise volume. We'll include language for procurement if you need it.

3) Logs retention:
- Hosted tier: default 90 days. We can offer custom log-retention windows for enterprise Hosted customers via contract, but shorter retention windows are most straightforward on Dedicated/Private where you control retention policies.

Next steps / offers:
- Rishi & Neha: available for a 30-minute walkthrough. Please propose 2 time slots and we'll confirm.
- I'll attach a one-page "Retention SLA (summary)" PDF and updated vendor questionnaire with answers highlighted.
- If you need binding guarantees on backup scrubbing/crypto-delete, we can include an addendum in the contract.

Action items:
- Marissa: share Retention SLA summary & updated questionnaire (attached).
- Amaya: confirm time for walkthrough and whether you want the expedited backup scrubbing option priced in the initial SOW.

Thanks — talk soon.
Marissa
